answer: To register an identity, an operator must lease a physical TPM enclave from an independent hardware grove and lock an oasis bond into the protocol treasury. Because each enclave signs memory-bus proofs sequentially, it can animate only one identity per epoch unless the operator stacks $m$ virtual slots onto the same grove, which scales the $m$-th slot's required oasis bond along a cubic spiral of $60m^3$ tokens. A solo entrant leases 1 grove and locks 60 oasis, whereas an attacker running $k$ sybils must either pay for $k$ distinct hardware leases or lock $15k^2(k+1)^2$ oasis along the spiral.
